qs.q: A 25-year-old man presents with progressive muscle weakness and is found to have a mutation in the dystrophin gene. Which best explains why this mutation leads to muscle damage?
o: Inhibition of key enzymes required for mitochondrial oxidation
Disruption of normal DNA repair mechanisms causing cell death
Defective structural protein disrupting muscle cell membrane stability
Accumulation of misfolded proteins within the endoplasmic reticulum
qs.e: Dystrophin is a structural protein anchoring the muscle cytoskeleton to the cell membrane, and its absence causes membrane fragility and progressive muscle damage. This is distinct from metabolic enzyme defects or DNA repair disorders.
qs.s: Genetics & Disease: Muscular Dystrophy, CF, Marfan, Diabetes, Cancer: MCQs

qs.q: A 5-year-old boy presents with progressive muscle weakness and is diagnosed with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). Which type of mutation in the dystrophin gene is responsible for this condition?
qs.e: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy is caused by a nonsense mutation that introduces a premature stop codon, leading to a truncated protein. A silent mutation would not alter the phenotype or cause such a severe condition.
qs.s: Types of Mutations in ARBHN: MCQs

qs.q: A 25-year-old man presents with progressive muscle weakness. Genetic testing reveals a mutation in the dystrophin gene on the X chromosome. Which best explains why this mutation leads to disease? Dystrophin anchors the cytoskeleton to the membrane; without it, muscle fibers tear during contraction. ---
o: Impaired immune surveillance against abnormal muscle fibers
Defective structural protein disrupting muscle cell membrane stability
Loss of DNA repair capacity leading to increased mutations
Defective enzyme causing substrate accumulation in lysosomes
Failure of apoptosis leading to accumulation of abnormal myocytes
qs.e: Dystrophin is a structural protein that anchors the cytoskeleton, and its absence destabilizes the muscle cell membrane.
